McLaren.summary: McLaren has fitted a new, low‑downforce rear wing that's been tuned specifically for this circuit’s layout. By reducing drag, the car can hit higher top‑speed on the long straights, giving the team a better chance to stay on the lead lap. In short, it’s a straight‑line speed boost that could be the difference between fighting for points or settling further back.

Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has tweaked the rear of the car – reshaping the suspension geometry and the little winglet on the rear corner – to give the car a more stable, bite‑ready feel through the bends. They’ve also trimmed the rear‑wing flap for this circuit, shaving off a bit of drag so the car can pull harder on the straights. Together, these changes should make the SF‑something feel tighter in corners while still keeping top‑end speed competitive for the weekend.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls have reshaped the front wing’s first two elements and added camber to the front‑suspension wishbone, giving the car a sharper front‑end bite and more consistent turn‑in. A merged, wider side‑pod inlet and a re‑shaped engine cover improve cooling reliability, while updates to the rear‑corner cascade, winglets and diffuser fine‑tune the rear airflow for better stability and a stronger rear‑end push. Finally, the rear wing’s new profiles give the team a wider drag window, letting them dial in the perfect balance for this weekend’s circuit.

Mercedes F1 Team.summary: Mercedes has lengthened a piece on the front‑wing endplate to smooth the airflow coming off the front of the car, giving it a little extra front‑end grip and stability into the corners. At the back, they’ve nudged the rear‑corner “drum” element inward, tweaking how the rear tire loads so the car can put down power more consistently without overheating the tyres. Together, these tweaks should help the team get better balance and traction right out of the gates for this weekend’s race.

Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has trimmed and reshaped its front wing and nose, giving the car a tighter, more balanced front end that will keep it glued to the track through the high‑speed corners. The rear wing now has a smaller upper element and the beam wing is a single‑piece, cutting drag so the car can hit the straight‑line speeds the weekend demands. In short, the aero tweaks sharpen the car’s handling and boost top‑end pace, giving the team a better shot at a strong qualifying and race performance.

Alpine F1 Team.summary: Alpine has fitted a low‑downforce rear wing and a matching low‑downforce beam wing, both tuned specifically for this circuit’s high‑speed layout. The slimmer aero set‑up reduces drag, giving the car more straight‑line speed and helping drivers carry more momentum through the fast corners. In short, Alpine’s tweak should make the car quicker on the straights and more competitive in this weekend’s speed‑focused race.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams has reshaped the forward floor fences and given the floor‑edge wing and its little “spat” a more intricate curve, while also tweaking a side‑pod inlet and the engine‑cover vent. These tweaks smooth the air flowing under and around the car, helping to generate a little extra down‑force and stability without compromising straight‑line speed. In short, the changes should give the drivers a tighter, more predictable feel on the corners this weekend.
